parsed.summary: As written, the Lean theorem claims that every group G : Type is finitely presented and not sofic. The name and the paper's content suggest the intended statement is existential: some finitely presented group is nonsofic. The ∀ makes the statement false (the trivial group is sofic), so it does not capture the intended result.

glossary.plain: Fraction of points of a finite set Y on which two permutations p, q differ: d_H(p,q)/|Y|.
A map G → Sym(n) with n>0 and identity sent to identity; it need not be a homomorphism.
glossary.standard_concept: map to a finite symmetric group used for sofic approximation
glossary.note: Only action 1 = 1 is required, which is harmless.

glossary.plain: For g,h in F, the permutation of gh is within ε of the product of the permutations of g and h. Each g ≠ 1 in F has normalized distance from the identity permutation greater than 1−ε.
glossary.note: Matches the paper's informal description: multiplication holds at almost every point, and non-identity elements move almost every point.

glossary.plain: For every finite F ⊆ G and every ε in (0,1), there is a permutation model that is good on F with parameter ε.
glossary.note: Stated for arbitrary groups, not only countable ones. This agrees with the standard definition.

glossary.plain: For every type G with a group structure, G is finitely presented and G is not sofic.
glossary.standard_concept: existence of a finitely presented nonsofic group
glossary.note: The quantifier is ∀ where ∃ is needed.

lean_claims.plain: For every group G in Type (the structure is bound as an explicit argument), G is finitely presented and not sofic. This is false: the trivial group is sofic, and infinite free groups are not finitely presented.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2)^× is not sofic.

coverage.why: No statement about the Leavitt unit group appears in the Lean file.

coverage.paper_ref: Existence of a finitely presented nonsofic group (a consequence not shown in the excerpt)
coverage.why: The Lean statement universally quantifies over all groups, which is false. An existential statement would be the faithful one. The existence claim itself is not in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: The statement is `∀ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ Sofic G`, where the name and the paper's content call for `∃ G, ∃ _ : Group G, ...`. As written it says every group is finitely presented and nonsofic. This is false: the trivial group is sofic, and ℤ is sofic. A proof of the statement as written would therefore imply False, so the Comparator check is vacuous or untrustworthy.
flags.probe_idea: Prove `¬ (∀ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ Sofic G)`, for example by showing `Sofic PUnit` (take the trivial permutation model). Compare with the intended `∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ Sofic G`.
